ordered_diagnoses: supratentorial hemangioblastoma at the anterior skull base

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction with highly vascularized mass
salient_findings: Voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
Hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Considerable uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy regarding rib and vertebral lesions
key_facts: Woman in her 30s with no relevant medical history
Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction
Endoscopic examination found a voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
CT scan showed a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, on the left thyroid, the fifth rib, and the L4 vertebra
MRI confirmed a hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Radioiodine scintigraphy found considerable uptake regarding rib and vertebral lesions
Sinonasal tumor had low uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy
Serum thyroglobulin was significantly elevated at 4432 ng/mL
Biopsy results confirmed VTC metastasis in both costal and sinonasal tumor biopsies

raw.rationale: The presence of a highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities, along with the findings from imaging studies and significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin, suggests a diagnosis that involves both vascular and possibly thyroid-related pathology, but the key factor here is the vascular nature and location of the tumors, which aligns more closely with a schwannoma given the description of the mass and its behavior.

rejected.why: Does not typically present with a fixed, pulsatile mass

rejected.label: angioedema
rejected.why: Characterized by transient swelling, not a fixed mass

rejected.label: supratentorial hemangioblastoma at the anterior skull base
rejected.why: While vascular, the description and location do not perfectly match the provided case facts, especially considering the involvement of the thyroid and other distant sites

rejected.label: benign nasal schwannoma
rejected.why: While closer, the term 'encapsulated sinonasal schwannoma' more specifically matches the description of a well-defined, vascular tumor in the sinonasal area
